ITQAN:v3p266/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.claim: The Qur'an favors the rarer of synonyms, such as ضيزى, الحطمة, سقر, لظى, and هاوية, often to preserve each surah's rhyme.
ITQAN:v3p266/r7.anchor: إيثار أغرب اللفظتين نحو ﴿ قسمة ضيزى ﴾ ولم يقل ( جائرة )

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.claim: Disbelievers mock the description of Hell because they presume to know everything, but it rests on divine wisdom: truth-seekers benefit and arrogant know-it-alls ruin their fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r3.anchor: Those who have the desire for the truth will benefit from it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats سأصليه سقر as a replacement for the threat سأرهقه صعودا; Abū Ḥayyān instead regards them as successive threats for obstinacy and then slandering the Qurʾān.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p330/r8.anchor: قال الزمخشري: بدل من سأرهقه صعودا

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r10.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r10.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r10.claim: ‘Saqar’ is diptote because it is a feminine proper name.
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r10.anchor: لا ينصرف لأنها معرفة، وهي مؤنثة

ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r11.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r11.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p246#2/r11.claim: Saqar is one of the names of Hell.

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies Saqar as the sixth level of Hell.
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس : { سقر } اسم للطبقة السادسة من جهنم

RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p178#3/r2.claim: Saqar is indeclinable because it is a proper name and feminine.

STUDYQURAN:74:26/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r1.speaker: Bg, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r1.claim: Some identify Saqar as a name for Hell.
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r1.anchor: According to some Saqar is one of the names of Hell

STUDYQURAN:74:26/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r2.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r2.claim: Others identify Saqar as the name of one of Hell’s gates.
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r2.anchor: according to others, the name of one of the gates of Hell

STUDYQURAN:74:26/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r3.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r3.claim: Some say Saqar has no derivation.
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r3.anchor: Some say it has no derivation

STUDYQURAN:74:26/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r4.speaker: Some commentators
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r4.claim: Others derive Saqar from saqarathu al-shams, the sun melting or scorching something.
STUDYQURAN:74:26/r4.anchor: while others say it derives from saqarathu al-shams, meaning, “the

TABATABAI:74:26-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r1.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r1.claim: Some say this threat confirms the preceding verse despite differing in meaning: both deny that the Qur’an is human speech, so the clauses are not coordinated.
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r1.anchor: قيل إن هذه الآية كالتأكيد للآية السابقة وإن اختلفتا معنى لأن المقصود منهما نفي كونه قرآنا من كلام الله

TABATABAI:74:26-30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r2.claim: God will make him enter Saqar, either a Qur’anic name for Hell or one of its levels.
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r2.anchor: أي سأدخله سقر وسقر من أسماء جهنم في القرآن أو دركة من دركاتها

TABATABAI:74:26-30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r3.claim: The clause explains or apposes the earlier threat to burden him with an arduous ascent.
TABATABAI:74:26-30/r3.anchor: وجمله { سأصليه سقر } بيان أو بدل من قوله { سأرهقه صعودا }

BURSEVI:v10p178/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r7.speaker: الصحاح
BURSEVI:v10p178/r7.claim: Al-Ṣiḥāḥ defines Saqar as one of the names of the Fire.
BURSEVI:v10p178/r7.anchor: لما قال في الصحاح سقر اسم من أسماء النار

BURSEVI:v10p178/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
BURSEVI:v10p178/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Saqar is Hell’s sixth level; the name is also connected to the sun burning and hurting someone.
BURSEVI:v10p178/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما اسم للطبقة السادسة من جهنم

BURSEVI:v10p178/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p178/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p178/r9.claim: Saqar is an inclusionary apposition for the earlier ṣaʿūd, whether hardships or a mountain of fire, since Saqar encompasses either.
BURSEVI:v10p178/r9.anchor: بدل من سأرهقه صعود أبدل الاشتمال سواء جعل مثلا لما يلقى من الشدائد

TABRISI:74:25-31/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:25-31/r3.claim: Saqar is Hell into which God will place him and keep him bound.

TABRISI:74:25-31/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r4.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:25-31/r4.claim: An alternative identifies Saqar as one level of Hell.
TABRISI:74:25-31/r4.anchor: وقيل: سقر دركة من دركات جهنم

TABRISI:74:25-31/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:25-31/r5.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:74:25-31/r5.claim: Another alternative identifies Saqar as a gate of Hell.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r4.claim: The threat means that God will make him enter the Fire; Saqar is a name for Hell and is indeclinable because it is definite and feminine.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r4.anchor: أي سأدخله النار، وسقر: اسم من أسماء جهنم. لا ينصرف للتعريف والتأنيث

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Saqar as the sixth layer of Hell.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p432/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس: وهي الطبق السادس من جهنم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r6.claim: God will admit him to Hell.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:74:21-27/r6.anchor: { سأصليه سقر } سأدخله جهنم، ثم أعلم عظم شأن سقر من العذاب، فقال:

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r1.claim: This verse explicates the earlier threat of Saud and is an inclusive substitute for it.
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r1.anchor: Bu âyet سَأُرْهِقُهُۥ صَعُودًا’den bedel-i iştimâldir ve onun mazmûnunu îzahtır

ELMALILI:74:26-31/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:26-31/r2.claim: Some call Saqar non-Arabic; Elmalılı prefers deriving it from sakr, the sun's scorching heat, giving it the sense of burning.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r4.speaker: Şevkânî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r4.claim: Saqar is a name for fire and denotes one of Hell’s sections with severe punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:18/r4.anchor: 26. âyette geçen “sekar” kelimesi ateşin isimlerinden olup cehennemin ağır cezalık kısımlarından birini ifade ettiği belirtilir (bk. Şevkânî, V, 377).

ITQAN:v4p378/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.speaker: author
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.claim: Ghayy, Atham, Mwbq, Saʿir, Wayl, Saʾil, and Suhaq are valleys in Hell.
ITQAN:v4p378/r7.anchor: وغي وأثام وموبق والسعير وويل وسائل وسحق أودية في جهنم

ITQAN:v4p378/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p378/r13.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v4p378/r13.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr calls Saʿir a valley of pus in Hell and Suhaq a valley in Hell.
ITQAN:v4p378/r13.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير قال السعير واد من قيح في جهنم وسحق واد في جهنم

FARRA:v3p202/r5.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p202/r5.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p202/r5.claim: سقر is a proper name for Hell and therefore is not declined; لظى is likewise a name.
FARRA:v3p202/r5.anchor: وهي اسم من أسماء جهنم، فلذلك لم يجز، وكذلك «لظى»

NAHHAS:v5p67/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r9.claim: Saqr is indeclinable because it is a feminine proper name, not because it is foreign; a three-letter foreign name with a moving middle normally declines.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r9.anchor: قيل لم ينصرف لأنها اسم لمؤنث وقيل إنها اسم أعجمي والأول الصواب

NAHHAS:v5p67/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p67/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p67/r10.claim: Saqr is Arabic-derived: the sun can scorch, and الساقور is heated iron used to cauterize a donkey.
NAHHAS:v5p67/r10.anchor: وأيضا فإنه اسم عربي مشتق يقال سقرته الشمس إذا أحرقته والساقور حديدة تحمى

SAMIN-DURR:74:26/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:26/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:74:26/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī parses this as substitution for سأرهقه صعودا; clear if صعود means hardship, difficult if it is a rock in Hell, except as part-whole since Hell contains it.
SAMIN-DURR:74:26/r1.anchor: هذا بدل من قوله: { سأرهقه صعودا } قاله الزمخشري. فإن كان المراد بالصعود المشقة فالبدل واضح

ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r2.claim: God will make him endure hell-fire in the life to come.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25/r2.anchor: I shall cause him to endure hell-fire

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r1.claim: Saqar is the earliest Qur'anic occurrence of this term and one of seven metaphorical names for afterlife suffering, which man brings on himself through sin and deliberate blindness to spiritual truths.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r1.anchor: one of the seven metaphorical names given in the Qur'an to the concept of the suffering in the hereafter which man brings upon himself by sinning and deliberately remaining blind and deaf, in this world, to spiritual truths

ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.claim: Asad reads this and Qur'anic descriptions of the hereafter allegorically, as the next verse and verses 28 onward indicate.
ASAD-NOTES:74:25#n13/r2.anchor: The allegorical character of this and all other Qur'anic descriptions of man's condition and destiny in the hereafter is clearly alluded to in the subsequent verse

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p63/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p63/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p63/r1.claim: The cited passages preserve charges that the Messenger was aided by others, copied ancient tales, was bewitched, or lacked angelic and worldly signs; the Quran answers by affirming revelation and God's knowledge and recalling earlier messengers.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p63/r1.anchor: وقال الذين كفروا إن هذا إلا إفك افتراه وأعانه عليه قوم آخرون فقد جاءوا ظلما وزورا

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r1.claim: “I will put him in Saqar” is a partitive substitution for “I will burden him with the ascent”: Saqar includes severe ordeals and, on one interpretation, a mountain of fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r1.anchor: سأصليه سقر بدل من سأرهقه الخ بدل اشتمال لاشتمال السقر على الشدائد وعلى الجبل من النار

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān treats the two threats as successive: the ascent answers his defiance of the signs, while Saqar answers his claim that the Qurʾān is transmitted magic.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r2.anchor: وقال أبو حيان يظهر أنهما جملتان أعتقبت كل واحدة منهما على سبيل توعد العصيان الذي قبل كل واحدة منهما

ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r3.claim: Al-Ālūsī notes that Abū Ḥayyān’s division is open to an evident objection in light of the preceding discussion.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p125/r3.anchor: وفيه بحث لا يخفى على من أحاط خبرا بما تقدم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r11.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r11.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r11.claim: Sa-uṣlīhi means 'I will make him enter'; Saqar is one of the names of Hell.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p269/r11.anchor: سأصليه} سأدخله {سقر} وسقر اسم من أسماء جنهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r8.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:20-28/r8.claim: The wording magnifies the dread of Saqar.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r1.claim: After describing his obstinacy and its punishment as Suud, the passage now details the afterlife recompense by naming Saqar.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r1.anchor: ولما انقضى بيان عناده فحصل التشوف لتفصيل جزائه في معاده , قال مبينا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r2.claim: Saqar is a fiery level whose intense heat attacks and melts the brain, answering the man’s own mental plotting to burn God’s friends.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r2.anchor: سقر * } أي الدركة النارية التي تفعل في الأدمغة من شدة حموها ما يجل عن الوصف

BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r3.claim: God will put him into Saqar under an inevitable threat that will come soon.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p229/r3.anchor: فأدخله إياه وألوحه في الشدائد حرها وأذيب دماغه بها

DURR-FULL:v8p331/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Saqar as the lowest part of Hell, containing the tree of Zaqqūm.
DURR-FULL:v8p331/r12.anchor: وأخرج ابن المنذر عن ابن عباس قال: {سقر} أسفل الجحيم نار فيها شجرة الزقوم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r1.claim: The sura describes Hell's terrors and the disbelievers' inability to escape punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r1.anchor:
ووصف أهوال جهنم .
والرد على المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p293/r4.claim: The passage makes the disbelievers despair of escaping punishment.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r1.claim: The fa in ‘then he said’ marks immediate succession: once the thought occurred after intense deliberation, he could not hold back from speaking.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r1.anchor: وعطف قوله : { فقال } بالفاء لأن هذه المقالة لما خطرت بباله بعد اكتداد فكره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r2.claim: ‘I shall burn him in Saqar’ begins a new explanatory sentence prompted by the preceding account of thought and calculation, or replaces ‘I shall burden him with a steep ascent.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r2.anchor: جملة { سأصليه سقر } مستأنفة استئنافا بيانيا ناشئا عن قوله : { إنه فكر وقدر }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r3.claim: Iṣlāʾ can mean experiencing fire's heat for warmth; al-Harith ibn Hilliza's poetry witnesses this sense through ṣilāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r3.anchor: وفعل صلي يطلق على إحساس حرارة النار ، فيكون لأجل التدفىء كقول الحارث بن حلزة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r4.claim: Hamid ibn Thawr's line ‘lā taṣṭalī al-nāra’ also uses the verb for warming oneself at a fire.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r4.anchor: وكما قال حميد بن ثور : لا تصطلي النار إلا مجمرا أرجا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r5.claim: Iṣlāʾ also means burning; Qur'anic examples include 111:3, 92:14–15, and the cited instances in Sura al-Nisaʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r5.anchor: ويطلق على الاحتراق بالنار قال تعالى : { سيصلى نارا ذات لهب في سورة أبي لهب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r6.claim: Saqar is a proper name for a level of Hell; many commentators use it as a synonym for Jahannam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r6.anchor: وسقر : علم لطبقة من جهنم ، عن ابن عباس : أنه الطبق السادس من جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Saqar as the sixth level of Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس : أنه الطبق السادس من جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r8.speaker: ابن عطية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAtiyya cites a report identifying Saqar as the sixth depth of Hell and confines his account to that explanation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r8.anchor: قال ابن عطية : سقر هو الدرك السادس من جهنم على ما روي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r9.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r9.claim: The majority of commentators explain Saqar as synonymous with Hell.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r9.anchor: وجرى كلام جمهور المفسرين بما يقتضي أنهم يفسرون سقر بما يرادف جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r10.claim: Saqar is diptote because it is a proper feminine name, for a place in Hell or Hell itself; feminine pronouns in 74:27 and 74:30 support this.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r10.anchor: وسقر ممنوع من الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث لأنه اسم بقعة من جهنم أو اسم جهنم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r11.speaker: الجواليقي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r11.claim: Al-Jawaliqi, as cited in al-Itqan, says Saqar is an Arabicized loanword without identifying its original form or language.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r11.anchor: وقيل سقر معرب نقله في ( الإتقان ) عن الجواليقي ولم يذكر الكلمة المعربة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r12.claim: ‘What will make you know what Saqar is?’ is a circumstantial clause modifying Saqar.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r12.anchor: و { ما أدراك ما سقر } جملة حالية من { سقر } ، أي سقر التي حالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r13.claim: The clause means no informant could make Saqar's reality known to the Prophet, magnifying its dreadful state.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p310/r13.anchor: أي سقر التي حالها لا ينبئك به منبىء وهذا تهويل لحالها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.claim: Another possibility is that هي refers to Saqar, which serves as a reminder through its threat and horrors; an omitted noun such as its mention or description is understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p319/r4.anchor: ويحتمل أن يرجع إلى سقر } ( المدثر : 26 ) وإنما تكون { ذكرى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r1.claim: Saqar is reported to be the sixth level of Hell.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r1.anchor: سقر هو الدرك السادس من جهنم على ما روي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r2.claim: أصليه means putting him into the Fire so he directly encounters its flames.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p395#3/r2.anchor: و «أصليه» معناه أجعله فيها مباشرا لنارها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#4/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#4/r1.claim: The threat means that God will admit him to the Fire; Saqar was discussed at 54:48.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p407#4/r1.anchor: سأصليه سقر أي سأدخله النار وقد ذكر سقر في سورة القمر 48

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r3.claim: Iṣlāʾ means consigning someone to the place of fire; its root sense is remaining or sticking there.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r3.anchor: الإصلاء: إلزام موضع النار، أصلاه يصليه إصلاء

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r4.claim: Saqar is an indeclinable feminine proper name for Hell, named from the sun's painful scorching of the brain; the name reflects the fire's intense pain.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r4.anchor: سقر: اسم من أسماء جهنم، ولا ينصرف؛ لأنه مؤنث معرفة

JISHUMI:v10p7161/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r5.claim: The related word saqr/sakr for a falcon uses the same root by analogy with the severity of its attack's pain.
JISHUMI:v10p7161/r5.anchor: ومنه: السقر والصقر بالسين والصاد: الجارحة

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r2.claim: After mentioning the disbeliever, the passage follows with a threat against him: God will consign him to Saqar.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r2.anchor: ثم عقب ذكر الكافر بالوعيد له، فقال سبحانه: سأصليه سقر

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r3.claim: God says He will bring the disbeliever into the fire and keep him there perpetually.

JISHUMI:v10p7162/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r4.claim: Saqar is variously described as one level of Hell, one of its gates, or one of its names.
JISHUMI:v10p7162/r4.anchor: سقر: قيل: درك من دركات جهنم، وقيل: باب من أبوابه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p652/r1.claim: سأصليه سقر replaces the earlier promise that he would endure Ṣaʿūd.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r12.claim: Saqr is a name for Hell, derived from the sun scorching and hurting the brain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p142/r12.anchor: أحدهما : أنه اسم من أسماء جهنم مأخوذ من قولهم : سقرته الشمس إذا آلمت دماغه , فسميت جهنم بذلك لشدة إيلامها .

MUQATIL:74:18-30/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r7.claim: Saqar is the fifth gate of Hell.
MUQATIL:74:18-30/r7.anchor: قول البشر سأصليه سقر } [آية: 26] يعني الباب الخامس من جهنم.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r1.claim: “I shall make him enter it” explains the earlier threat “سأرهقه سعودا”.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r2.claim: Saqar is the proper name of Hell and is diptote because it is a feminine proper noun.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p296#2/r2.anchor: علم لجنهم ولم ينصرف للتعريف والتأنيث

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r1.claim: God will put the threatened person into Saqar to suffer its heat.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r1.anchor: أي سأدخله سقر كي يصلى حرها

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r2.claim: Saqar is named from the sun melting, scorching, and burning skin; it is indeclinable because definite and feminine.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r2.anchor: وإنما سميت سقر من سقرته الشمس: إذا أذابته ولوحته

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies Saqar as the sixth level of Hell.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هي الطبق السادس من جهنم

QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r4.speaker: النبي
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r4.claim: Abu Hurayra reports Moses asking God which servant was poorest; God replied, the inhabitant of Saqar. Al-Thaʿlabi gives no grading.
QURTUBI-FULL:74:26-29/r4.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:
